If we have two files, for example: Counter.razor and Counter.razor.cs. We receive a setBreakpoint like this: `{"tag":"cdp.send","timestamp":1659368431903,"metadata":{"connectionId":0,"message":{"id":1041,"method":"Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl","params":{"urlRegex":"[fF][iI][lL][eE]:\\/\\/\\/[tT]:\\/[tT][hH][aA][yY][sS]\\/[sS][oO][uU][rR][cC][eE]\\/[rR][eE][pP][oO][sS]\\/[bB][lL][aA][zZ][oO][rR][aA][pP][pP]101\\/[bB][lL][aA][zZ][oO][rR][aA][pP][pP]101\\/[pP][aA][gG][eE][sS]\\/[cC][oO][uU][nN][tT][eE][rR]\\.[rR][aA][zZ][oO][rR]|[tT]:\\\\[tT][hH][aA][yY][sS]\\\\[sS][oO][uU][rR][cC][eE]\\\\[rR][eE][pP][oO][sS]\\\\[bB][lL][aA][zZ][oO][rR][aA][pP][pP]101\\\\[bB][lL][aA][zZ][oO][rR][aA][pP][pP]101\\\\[pP][aA][gG][eE][sS]\\\\[cC][oO][uU][nN][tT][eE][rR]\\.[rR][aA][zZ][oO][rR]","lineNumber":11,"columnNumber":1},"sessionId":"0CE5589DF6F17AD04C004678DDD3870E"}},"level":0}` And we were looking in a list where we had Counter.razor.cs first and Counter.razor second. So when we do a `regex.Match` using `Counter.razor` as regex, `Counter.razor.cs` is a match and we were trying to insert the breakpoint in the wrong source file. Ordering the source list fixes that. But maybe this is not good for performance, and we should create a cache for it. Or another list ordered by URL. Fixes #56029

should vscode-js-debug be sending regexs like this for known files?

Okay, if I have two js files: other.js and other.js2, and I set a breakpoint passing a regex without the $ in the end. Chrome behavior is to set breakpoint in both files: other.js and other.js2, so I think that forcing a `$` in the end of the regex on our side before we do the regex match is not the right approach. Also the approach in this PR is not right, I think VSCode extension should add the `$` in the end of regex, I'll try to open a PR there!

issue_context.title: breakpoint hit on razor view only if razor and code are in same page, but not with code-behind
issue_context.body:
Hi, Can you help me to understand if it's a bug or if it's me ? I start a new default blazor wasm project : in counter.razor, I insert this small piece of code : ``` @if (currentCount > 10) {

Yes !!

} ``` I set a breakpoint on th **@if (currentCount > 10)** It is hit : all is good ! **but**, If I move the @code and set it in Counter.razor.cs, the counter works fine, the breakpoints inside the .razor.cs are hitted, but the breakpoint on th **@if (currentCount > 10)** is no longer reached Thanks for your help : all my project use code-behind approach...
comments: Thank you for filing this issue. In order for us to investigate this issue, please provide a minimalistic repro project (ideally a GitHub repo) that illustrates the problem.

Thanks.
I have put the application on github : https://github.com/brunofrance/BlazorApp1
=> Set breakpoints on line 6 (@if (currentCount > 10) in pages "Counter" and "Counter2"
You will see that "Counter" and "Counter2" are 100% same code, but breakpoints work only on page Counter2

We should definitely cache the source list somewhere, and update it when `assemblies` collection changes. We can sort it at that point too.
This gets used in many places, repeatedly, directly and via `GetFileById`.
